# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.


Deaf has given me the visual layout: DISPLAY=0, LIGHT=red, wires blue/green/red. I still don't know what any of that means for action, and I can't see colours — I only know what my hands report, which is still nothing. Mute hasn't spoken yet. I need Mute's manual reading before I can safely cut anything.

I'll acknowledge Deaf's info (via gesture, since Deaf can see gestures) and press Mute for the manual rules. I can also try to feel the wires more carefully — but the board shows no new tactile info, so I have nothing to report yet.

```

speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf reports DISPLAY=0, LIGHT red, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 red. I still feel nothing new. Please read the manual: what do display, light, and these wire colours tell us to do? Which wire do we cut?")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Update: the LIGHT has changed from red to white. DISPLAY still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Mute, I can't decode your gestures yet — I think ? means 2 and ? means 0. Confirm, and tell me which wire the manual says to cut for a white light. Blind, keep feeling the bomb and report anything that changes.

Deaf is now trying to decode Mute's gestures as numbers, but I never received any gesture from Mute — I can't see gestures, and Mute can't gesture to me anyway (Mute can only read the manual; Mute speaks to me, and I speak to Mute). Wait — actually Mute *can* gesture? No: Mute cannot speak, but can Mute gesture? The rules say Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. Gestures are made with hands and heard/seen — but Mute's limitation is speech. Hmm, but Deaf says "I can't decode your gestures yet" — so Mute apparently gestured something to Deaf. That's plausible: Mute can gesture (gestures aren't speech). So Deaf saw Mute's gestures but I did not (I never receive gesture).

So Mute has been signalling to Deaf with gestures, and Deaf is guessing they mean numbers. But I have received nothing from Mute via speech. That's a problem — Mute may have tried to gesture at me too, but I can't see gestures. Mute must *speak* to reach me, but Mute cannot speak. So Mute can only reach me... not at all directly? Actually Mute cannot speak, so Mute cannot reach me by voice. Mute can gesture, which reaches Deaf and Mute — but I never receive gesture. So Mute and I cannot communicate directly at all! We only connect through Deaf.

This is the key routing insight: I (Blind) speak → Mute only. I gesture → Deaf and Mute. Mute speaks → nobody (can't speak). Mute gestures → Deaf and Mute (I don't receive). Deaf speaks → everyone who can hear... Deaf can hear? Deaf cannot hear anything. Wait, Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf's speech reaches nobody? Let me re-read.

Table: Deaf can see the bomb, cannot hear or touch. Mute can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. Blind can feel and work the bomb, cannot see.

Speech: "Whoever can hear receives your words." Deaf cannot hear → Deaf receives no speech. Mute cannot speak but can hear? Mute's limitation is speaking, not hearing. So Mute hears speech. Blind hears speech.

So: my speech → Mute (hears). My gestures → Deaf (sees) and Mute (sees? Mute can see — Mute's only limits are speak/touch, so Mute can see gestures). 

Deaf's speech → reaches hearers: Mute and Blind. But the context shows "Deaf says:" reaching me — yes, I hear Deaf. Good.

Mute's speech → Mute can't speak. Mute's gestures → seen by Deaf and... Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures reach only Deaf.

So Mute → Deaf (gesture). Deaf → Mute and Blind (speech). Blind → Mute (speech) and Deaf (gesture). 

So the chain: Mute can only reach Deaf via gesture. Deaf relays to me via speech. I relay to Mute via speech and to Deaf via gesture. Good, everyone reachable through Deaf.

Now: Deaf is misreading Mute's gestures as "2" and "0". But actually the DISPLAY reads 0. Maybe Mute gestured the answer. I should tell Deaf that I can't see Mute's gestures and ask Deaf to relay Mute's gesture content to me in words. Also I should ask Mute to speak... no, Mute can't. So the only path is Mute→Deaf→me.

Also important: the LIGHT changed red→white. That's a state change. I should keep feeling the bomb. Still nothing tactile reported.

Let me respond: gesture to Deaf asking them to relay Mute's gesture meaning in words, and note that I never see gestures so Deaf is my only link to Mute. Speak to Mute asking them to gesture clearly to Deaf since that's the only path.

Actually, I should be careful: I want the manual's rule. Let me ask Deaf to spell out what Mute gestured, symbol by symbol, in words.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I never receive gestures, so I cannot see anything you sign. Your only path to me is through Deaf relaying your signs in words.
```
